about: Lesson 10 (T10, 10-write-it-down). Prairie Town is fictional; its plants, costs, CO2 rates and the CO2 cap are illustrative. The hour is 19:00 of lesson 0's real day (3 September 2025, SPP shapes from EIA-930 in town_year.json), cut and rounded exactly as lesson 0 does; the gas the hour needs (demand minus nuclear, wind and sun) comes out of that day, not from this file.
capNote: CO2 cap for the hour in tonnes: illustrative, chosen slack at the given demand (and still feasible up to about 230 MW of gas) so the reader can tighten it.

bins.label: Given
bins.sub: data it takes as it is

cards.why: the operator sets it every hour: it is what the model chooses.
the town uses what it uses; the model must meet demand, not choose it.

cards.text: The day's total running cost, as low as possible
cards.why: this is what the model tries to make smallest.
it must hold in every hour; no plan may break it.

cards.text: Wind and sun available, each hour
cards.why: the weather sets it; the model can spill some but cannot add more.
the operator chooses it, like the combined-cycle's output.
a limit that every plan must obey.

cards.text: Running cost per MWh of each plant
cards.why: fixed numbers ($40 and $100 per MWh) that weight the goal; the model does not choose them.

cards.text: The combined-cycle changes at most 40 MW an hour
cards.why: a rule that links each hour to the next.

cards.text: Spilled wind and sun, each hour
cards.why: when there is too much power the operator chooses how much to spill, within what the weather gives.
